answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is proof of costly work tied to a unique stake. Each agent must lock a bond before it can vote or claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if its outputs are repeatedly rejected by peers. Creating thousands of fake identities then means locking thousands of bonds, so the attacker pays real capital for every identity. Peers also cross-check answers, so a swarm of clones producing the same zenith, umber, and ferrous wording gets flagged as duplicates and loses its stake.
